title: Would you be little forgiving to not perfect games?
author: adolphite
selftext:
Since trying my hands on making games with AI (not that I have been successful), I have come to realize that game design and eventual shipping is so hard.

Even with AI, I can't seem to get some things right. It got me thinking about how people have made huge open world or complex games without AI in the past.

Are you now willing to give people some slack given the difficulty of making games or you expect them now not to make mistakes given that there's now AI to catch lots of bugs or coding errors?

comments.author: frigginwizard420
comments.body:
dont worry about it  

Make something you like, if other people like it, great  

If you're just into it for the $$, dont bother

comments.author: cowman3456
comments.body:
Mistakes = rushing out a cheap product. 

That's exactly what everybody hates.  If you want to build non-slop, put in the effort.

replies.author: maxneuds
replies.body:
That's it.
With a good idea and proper planning and definitions it's possible to get a good game even from one prompt and some hours of work, but unlikely. Depends a lot also on what assets are needed.

I spend most of my time actually working on assets. That's tough. And for anything with an actual world I find myself that neither 2D nor 3D world by AI is good, that's needs to be hand crafted.

replies.author: TheHaunterX
replies.body:
Confirmo 
Hice el loop, sistemas y tienda de mi juego en dos meses y llevo como 5 intentando hacer assets que encajen bien

comments.author: Putrid_Clue_2127
comments.body:
My standards for games now aren't really any different than they used to be. If it's fun and doesn't have weird things that break immersion, that's a pretty great start. 

This may sound dumb, but have you tried explaining to the ai you're using what your problem is, and then asking you to help come up with a gameplan for how it could potentially be fixed. Sometimes this gets it thinking about the problem differently itself. 

As someone else has already said, make a game that you'd want to play. Make it FOR you. Then if you like it and get actual gameplay from it, iron out the kinks until it's done and then see if anyone else likes it too. Don't ship it out just to ship it.

I'm currently working on a game I've wanted for years on mobile. It's for me. If others like it, that's great to! But I'm making it to my own gameplay standard. So it's got hundreds of hours of my own time in development so far, and probably about the same amount of time left to go. I'll just be happy when it feels like it's done for me.

comments.author: Big_Birthday_1846
comments.body: it’s not about perfection it’s just them being soulless asf, but you don’t need ai for that, just look at the mainstream industry

comments.author: dedaistgeil
comments.body: Make a good game, it's always about making a good game. A good game needs lots and lots of iteration, testing and polish. Doesn't matter if you use AI or not. AI does not mean you can sit back, type 1 prompt and have the next Skyrim. Even a simple game needs a lot of work with AI to become a marketable product. AI makes the entry easier but the development itself is still hard and takes time.

comments.author: DuckAndQwack
comments.body:
1) It's hard to say, that any of the games are perfect
2) No. If a game is bad (For me) — I won't play in it. If I feel the game good enough — I will play in it

comments.author: Agile_Branch_8743
comments.body:
AI is a tool that supports your existing skills. If you don't know a lot about game design, art direction, coding, etc., AI can't get things right for you.

Most big open world games are built by big teams that combine many different skillsets, usually dedicated to a very specific thing in the game (like artists focusing on trees or stones; not a joke, by the way), with people specialized in helping put all of that together. Then a bunch of people specialized in coming up with the game's concept before any development is done. People dedicated to selling the game.

AI can help you learn from those games, and if you know how to guide it, it can help tackle big chunks of the work. If you don't know what you're doing, I strongly believe AI can make things more difficult for you. Good luck fixing and making all those "omg guys I built this complete game in 3 days" builds fun; it's probably easier to start from scratch.

>Are you now willing to give people some slack given the difficulty of making games

I've always given creators slack. I give less slack to: a) AAA companies releasing incomplete games at full price; b) shovelware, including many of those AI one-shot guys I mentioned.

comments.author: _HoundOfJustice
comments.body: It depends on what exactly we talk about. There are no perfect games. However im very critical of games that are soulless and eventually fully driven by AI with little to none creative footprint and basically typical AI slop. Also people getting overconfident with AI and thinking they gotta build a large scoped game only to make it look empty, bugged as hell, boring are a problem too and their games deserve to be dunked on.

comments.author: Albius
comments.body: Honestly – no. With bigger supply then ever there’s never enough time for all the games. So quality becomes even more of a filter then ever

replies.author: Aligyon
replies.body:
Yup thats what i am noticing more and more. New IPs have a hell of a tough time unless you market it to very niche players, even then quality still is a big influence. 

Established IPs really has quiality plus years of updates and extra content in them so that's going to be a hard sell for people to buy ones game when with the same price you could buy No man sky or some other game that has vast content and polish

comments.author: Gelinhir
comments.body: If it's free it sok if it's paid why would you even

comments.author: PositiveScarcity8909
comments.body: No, I expect high quality and I don't care how you achieve it.

comments.author: daddy_reloaded
comments.body: It's clearly one of the most important things right now in game development. If your game isn't enough polished on realize (even early access) you will get refunds and bad notation and then good luck...

comments.author: romansamurai
comments.body:
It’s the opposite. The difficulty of making games has been reduced. Why would more slack be given now when it’s so much easier to design games. The pro form you’re running into is the realization that just having Claude make your game for you isn’t as easy as many people think. Getting past the concept stage and getting the design you want the way you want and then tuning that game and its systems, mechanics and balancing is incredibly difficult and time consuming. 

But that’s what separates great games from slop. Whether it’s with AI or not.

comments.author: Prestigious_Fee_2468
comments.body: It doesn't matter what u do or how some parts are under developed. What matters the most is if ur game is the right price and worth the time of playing.. there are very great AAA games, if ur game isn't AAA don't price it at the AAA cost

comments.author: Upbeat-Mail7201
comments.body: Nope not really sorry. You have the time like everyone else, and the power to put effort in. AI can not only help you making the game it can also teach you stuff to make a better game on your own with help. The result must be good on all ends, the tools used don't matter to me :) you either know your work or not

comments.author: lemming1607
comments.body:
Easier to make games should equal higher standard for gameplay.

It should be a complete game. AI can now fill in for everything youre not good at, and it needs to perform well, have fun gameloops, and be a complete experience.

We shouldn't lower our standards just cause people want to ship slop

AI raises the performance and quality bar for what will get bought

comments.author: Ok-Sea300
comments.body:
I think tolerance for mistakes is down, people expect high quality and label anything thats not percieved as excellent AI slop.

Even the poor bastards that hand make everything now are being belittled and called an AI slop artist for a few things being out of place.

Making games is hard man, there is so much to it that no one ever expects because the subtle details are what delivers the feeling and immersion, you feel them when you play but you never think about them until you try making a game.

AI helps overcome technical challenges, it is not a magic wand and "make no mistakes" is never going to work in a prompt because no one defined the mistakes to avoid.

comments.author: DancinFool82
comments.body: That's why game development takes a big team and years to complete. Ideas are cheap getting something stable and fun is a lot more difficult. I spent 20 years in games as a programmer and landing the plane trying to get the bugs to an acceptable number at the end of a project is a marathon.

comments.author: Chocoweb88
comments.body:
Dear OP, I think 1 aspect we need to consider is that this sub are mostly experienced designer/developers, or experienced gamers who play lots of game and has high standard. So I think the main responses here will have more expectations for a game. And I believe since everyone will be busy designing their own games + play the actually polished good games that they like, most people will not have time nor the needs to play a non-perfect game.

Though I believe if your game has really unique ideas + you spent real effort to make it work and fun to play, some people will appreciate it.

For my personal answer: I already investing all my time for my own game dev too, so I dont really have time to play some games that I enjoy, and thus I dont think I will have time to play others' in development game too 😅 but 1 thing I would happy to do is similar to r/playtester fashion, where we tryout each other games and give constructive feedback. So there's that. Good luck on your game!

comments.author: Matilozano96
comments.body:
There’s no perfect games.

Except Factorio.

comments.author: DeanRayGames
comments.body:
Some of the best games in the world have a fair bit of jank, bugs, etc. But what a good game must have is being INFECTIOUS. It has to get inside your head and make you WANT TO KEEP PLAYING. 

Having a lot of polish is important, though! Don't get lazy and think people will just forgive you for sloppiness.
